correctness.rationale: The exact same-model characteristic transform of Boyer–Majumdar is an explicit prior input. For z near 0, its slow Kummer branch has exponent a_-(z)=λ_-(z)/(r+λ_-(z)) and analytic amplitude c_- (r+λ_-)^{-a_-}/Γ(1-a_-). The second branch has a strictly greater positive real decay exponent near 0, so locally uniform Kummer asymptotics permit four derivatives by Cauchy formula. Writing x=(vz/γ)², expand -a_-(z)=x/(2p)+(2-p)x²/(8p²)+…, and the analytic log-amplitude to x². The fourth derivative yields coefficient 3(2-p)L/p² and constant (15p²−12γ_E p−24−2π²+24γ_E)/(4p²) in v⁴/γ⁴ units. At p=2 this is (18−π²)/8>0; variance is v²/γ²[(L+γ_E)/p−1/2]+o(1), giving the claimed normalized 1/log² law. Independent SymPy expansion checked the fourth coefficient and the residual. No finite-time sign statement or uniform p→2 joint limit is proved.

final_claim: For symmetrically initialized telegraph motion that uniformly resets both position and velocity to a previously visited state, the leading fourth cumulant changes sign at p=r/γ=2. At p=2, its log-time term vanishes and the unscaled fourth cumulant converges to v⁴(18−π²)/(8γ⁴), with standardized excess kurtosis asymptotic to (18−π²)/(2log²(rt)).
limitations: Requires symmetric initial velocity, uniform historical resetting of both position and velocity, positive fixed v,r,γ.
Only long-time fixed-parameter κ4 and variance, not all-order Gaussian rates, finite-time sign changes, or a uniform near-critical window.
